4.5. Classically, a modular form of weight k and level n is a holomorphic function f on the Poincaré half-plane

X = {z | Im(z) > 0}

satisfying the following conditions.

(A) If (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, ℤ) is congruent to (1 0; 0 1) mod n,

f(z) = (cz+d)⁻ᵏ f((az+b)/(cz+d)).

This condition implies that, for γ ∈ SL(2, ℤ/n), the image of γ₀ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL(2, ℤ), the function

f|γ₀ : z ↦ (cz+d)⁻ᵏ f((az+b)/(cz+d))

depends only on γ, not on the choice of γ₀. It is denoted f|γ.

(B) For every γ ∈ SL(2, ℤ/n),

(f|γ)(z) remains bounded as Im(z) → ∞

(it is equivalent, and more honest, to require f|γ to have polynomial growth in vertical strips as Im(z) → ∞).

Such a function is periodic with period n and therefore has a Fourier-series expansion

f(z) = ∑ aₘ e^(2πimz)    (m ∈ (1/n)ℤ, m ≥ 0).

Construction 4.6. Modular forms of weight k and level n are identified with the sections

H⁰(𝓜ₙ ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ, ω⊗ᵏ) = H⁰(𝓜ₙ, ω⊗ᵏ) ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ.

Proof. Suppose first that n ≥ 3. In that case, 𝓜ₙ ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ = Mₙ ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ is a scheme. The analytic space underlying Mₙ° ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ is

X/Ker(SL(2, ℤ) → SL(2, ℤ/n)),

and the holomorphic sections of ω⊗ᵏ on this space are identified with the holomorphic functions on X satisfying 4.5 (A). The analytic space underlying Mₙ ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ is obtained from it by adding finitely many points. A holomorphic section of ω⊗ᵏ on Mₙ° ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ extends to Mₙ ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ if and only if it satisfies (B). By GAGA, these sections are the algebraic sections of ω⊗ᵏ on Mₙ ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ.

The case of arbitrary n is reduced to the preceding one by passing to the invariants under

Ker(SL(2, ℤ/3n) → SL(2, ℤ/n))

in the space of modular forms of weight 3n. One could also invoke GAGA for the algebraic stack 𝓜ₙ ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ.

4.7. For n ≥ 3, (Mₙ ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ)ᵃⁿ is also the analytic space classifying generalized elliptic curves C/S over analytic spaces S, equipped with a level-n structure α such that det(α) = 1. From this point of view, a modular form f is a rule that assigns to every such curve a section of ω⊗ᵏ over S. The Fourier-series expansion is then obtained by evaluating the form on the Tate curve (4.3) (and multiplying the result by a power of 2πi depending on the normalizations chosen). For φ ∈ H⁰(Mₙ ⊗_{ℤ[ζₙ]} ℂ, ω⊗ᵏ), compatibility 4.4 shows that this expansion coincides with the expansion defined purely algebraically in § 3.
